items.summary: Mention @Computer in a Slack thread and the Calvin gateway spins up a Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode session for the task, each isolated in a rootless Podman container, with the result landing as a pull request. The whole stack fits on a single self-hosted VM, recommended to allow outbound-only networking. Apache-2.0.
items.title: OpenComputer: an open-source Devin alternative that takes tasks in Slack, one isolated computer per task (Show HN, Nov 20)

items.summary: A local inference server for Apple Silicon, built for agents rather than chat: it batches requests from many agents and runs them about 3x faster than mlx-lm; tool calls are validated against their grammar on the GPU, so they always parse; long prompts are cached on disk, so the next turn of a 138,000-token conversation starts in 2.4 seconds. One command connects OpenCode, Claude Code, OpenClaw and more. Apache-2.0; nothing leaves your Mac.
items.title: Locals: a local inference server for agents on your Mac, up to ~3x faster than mlx-lm with many agents at once (now runs Inkling 2 Mini)

items.summary: A small desktop agent plus an Android app turns a spare phone into a live panel for your computer: over a hundred widgets show system stats, Claude, Codex and Antigravity quotas and sessions, and you can answer Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode permission prompts with Allow / Deny right from the phone. Pairs over USB or Wi-Fi, with Tailscale support and Wake-on-LAN. MIT licensed, no account or cloud service.
items.title: PhoneBox: turn an old Android phone into a desk panel for your computer, and approve coding agents' permission prompts from the phone (v0.9.27, Nov 21)
